raw_response:
I am already old, so this year I will not do anything too aggressive. On my 8 mu, I will keep the familiar pattern: 5 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 3 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize are still my steady income, and cotton gives me another way to spread risk. Some people in the family work outside, so labor at home is not as free as before. Because of that, I will stay with the crops and methods I know well, use machine or hired help at the tight times, and not chase very high input. The extension man usually talks about standard rates, but on my land I still go a little by how the crop looks. For wheat, I will put a solid base fertilizer and then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks a bit weak. Maize has a tight turnaround after wheat harvest, so I will use simple tillage and sow quickly, otherwise I lose moisture and time. Cotton I will keep on the smaller block because it needs more watching and picking. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate wheat first, maize only if summer rain is short, and cotton just enough to hold it. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go yellow, but I still need to leave cash in hand, so I am not pushing the rates too high.
